item.title: Arsenal hold off energetic Sunderland to continue perfect title defence
item.description: Arsenal maintain their 100% start to their Premier League season with a win at Sunderland, who mount an admirable push for a point before Bukayo Saka's penalty puts the result beyond doubt.

item.title: Hull remain unbeaten in league after impressive Chelsea draw
item.description: In-form striker Joao Pedro scores a second-half equaliser as Chelsea rescues a point at home to promoted Hull City.

item.title: Jesus snatches late win for Forest as Villa's poor start continues
item.description: Igor Jesus scores an 88th minute winner as Nottingham Forest beat Aston Villa at Villa Park for the first time in 32 years and gives Oliver Glasner his first victory as Forest head coach since taking charge in the summer.

item.title: Flemming's late strike earns Ipswich win over 10-man Crystal Palace
item.description: Zian Flemming scores his first goal for Ipswich to give the club a late victory over 10-man Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park.

item.title: Brentford hold Bournemouth as Rose's wait for a win continues
item.description: Marco Rose's wait for a first Premier League victory as Bournemouth head coach continues as they are held to a 2-2 draw by Brentford at Vitality Stadium.

item.title: Fulham take first point of the season at lacklustre Liverpool
item.description: Fulham claim their first Premier League point of the season after a difficult start under Alvaro Arbeloa, as Liverpool fail to score for the first time this season just days after their Champions League victory over Atletico Madrid.

item.title: Tottenham's wait for league goal continues after Everton draw
item.description: Tottenham's wait for a first Premier League goal and win this season continues after Roberto de Zerbi's side were held to a goalless home draw by Everton.

item.title: 'Today the game was unprotected' - Arteta fumes but Arsenal survive
item.description: Arsenal produced a gritty 2-0 win against Sunderland, but Mikel Arteta fumed about the penalty that could have cost his side a result.

item.title: Toothless Spurs blank again as new era turns into a false dawn
item.description: Toothless Spurs' draw a blank again and are now in danger of seeing a brave new era turn into a false dawn, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.

item.title: Guimaraes and Raya crucial - Sunderland v Arsenal player ratings
item.description: How Sunderland and Arsenal players rated following their Premier League match.

item.title: More dropped points at Anfield - is it too early for Liverpool to worry?
item.description: Liverpool have failed to win either of their first two Premier League games at Anfield. But is it too early to worry?

item.title: New system, same problems - Alonso not happy with 'soft' Chelsea
item.description: It was subdued at Stamford Bridge after Chelsea's 2-2 draw with newly promoted Hull City.

item.title: Emery left searching for answers after another Villa loss
item.description: Aston Villa have lost three of their opening four Premier League games to leave boss Unai Emery struggling for answers.

item.title: Arsenal monitoring Como's Paz - Sunday's gossip
item.description: Arsenal are monitoring Nico Paz, Liverpool and Aston Villa are tracking Cher Ndour and Sunderland are refusing to give up on Geny Catamo, plus more.

item.title: Pickford joins Premier League clean sheet 100 club
item.description: Our Ask Me Anything team look at which goalkeepers have achieved 100 Premier League clean sheets.

item.title: Signed instead of Rashford, Gordon is proving worth at Barca
item.description: Anthony Gordon's £70m move to Barcelona was questioned by some - but the England winger is already proving his worth for the free-scoring Spanish giants.

item.title: Arteta 'very worried & very sad' over penalty incident
item.description: Mikel Arteta is pleased with Arsenal's performance against Sunderland, but is "very worried and very sad" about the penalty awarded to their opponents during the match at the Stadium of Light.

item.title: Referee 'completely wrong' to award penalty - Williams
item.description: Match of the Day pundits Ashley Williams and Thomas Frank believe Sunderland should not have been awarded a penalty after Ezri Konsa was adjudged to foul Dan Ballard, instead claiming that Arsenal should have had a free kick.

item.title: 'A clear red card' - Emery berates VAR as Villa lose late to Forest
item.description: Aston Villa manager Unai Emery was left frustrated with the match officials after they chose to not send off Nottingham Forest's James McAtee, following a challenge on Ian Maatsen which left the defender injured and meant Villa had to play the closing stages of the match with 10 men, with Forest taking advantage, scoring late to win 2-1 at Villa Park.

item.title: West Ham shock new-look London City
item.description: West Ham United earn their first win of the WSL season, holding on to beat a highly-touted London City Lionesses side at home.

item.title: We got what we deserved - Alonso on draw with Hull
item.description: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso admits his side "got what they deserved" as they drew 2-2 against Hull City at Stamford Bridge.

item.title: Chelsea's defence looks 'weak & disjointed' - analysis
item.description: Match of the Day pundit Ashley Williams says Chelsea's "struggling" defence looked "weak and disjointed" in their 2-2 draw against Hull at Stamford Bridge.
